def solve(nums):
    # Find the first index from the right where nums[i] < nums[i+1]
    n = len(nums)
    if n <= 1:
        return nums[:]
    i = n - 2
    while i >= 0 and nums[i] >= nums[i + 1]:
        i -= 1
    if i == -1:
        # Last permutation – return sorted order
        return sorted(nums)
    # Find the smallest element greater than nums[i] to the right
    j = n - 1
    while nums[j] <= nums[i]:
        j -= 1
    # Swap and reverse the suffix
    res = nums[:]
    res[i], res[j] = res[j], res[i]
    res[i + 1:] = list(reversed(res[i + 1:]))
    return res

def solve(nums):
    """Return the next lexicographic permutation of the list of integers.
    If the input is the highest permutation, return the sorted (lowest) permutation.
    The original list is not modified; a new list is returned.
    """
    # Make a copy to avoid mutating input
    a = list(nums)
    n = len(a)
    # Find the first index i from the right such that a[i] < a[i+1]
    i = n - 2
    while i >= 0 and a[i] >= a[i + 1]:
        i -= 1
    if i == -1:
        # Already the highest permutation
        return sorted(a)
    # Find the smallest element greater than a[i] to the right of i (scan from right)
    j = n - 1
    while a[j] <= a[i]:
        j -= 1
    # Swap a[i] and a[j]
    a[i], a[j] = a[j], a[i]
    # Reverse the suffix starting at i+1
    a[i + 1 :] = reversed(a[i + 1 :])
    return a

    res = []

        visited.add((r, c))
